summary: Petition under Section 79(1)(b) read with Section 79(1)(f) and Section 19 of Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulations 9, 19 and 20 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Trading License and other related matters) Regulations, 2020, inter alia, seeking a direction seeking a direction to the Respondent to pay the outstanding amount of Rs. 11,22,05,158 to the Petitioner against the power supplied by the Petitioner to the Respondent. The Petitioner, D.B. Power Limited (DBPL), has filed the present Petition under Sections 79(1) and 19 of the Electricity Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Act’) read with Regulations 9, 19 and 20 of the Central Electricity Regulatory Commission (Procedure, Terms and Conditions for Grant of Trading License and other related matters) Regulations, 2020 (hereinafter referred to as ‘the Trading Licence Regulations 2020’), against the Respondent on account of willful and prolonged failure on its part to clear the dues of the Petitioner for the power supplied by the Petitioner. - _b) Pass an Order initiating appropriate proceedings under Section 19 of the Electricity Act, 2003 read with Regulation 20 of the Trading License Regulations for revocation of the inter- State trading license granted to the Respondent;_ - _d) Pending final adjudication of the present Petition, pass an ex-parte ad interim order, directing Respondent No. 1 to forthwith secure and make payment of the amount in terms of prayer (a) above; and_ - a) The Respondent has paid a total amount of Rs 13,78,06,403/- to the Petitioner till 14.12.2021, leaving the outstanding balance of Rs 7,08,98,749/- for c) The Respondent has time and again acknowledged in writing to the Petitioner about the outstanding amount towards the tariff for supply of power made to the Respondent, and also restructured the payment plan thereof as under: d) From the above, it is evident that the Respondent, having received the power, had failed to fulfill its obligation to pay the tariff against the supply made and continues to be in default. It is further evident that the default by the Respondent is willful. It has been learnt that the power supplied by the Petitioner was supplied onwards by the Respondent to Haryana Discoms and the Respondent has been paid in full by the Haryana Discoms for such supply & despite this the Respondent is not discharging its liability to the Petitioner, which clearly establishes the _mala fide_ conduct of the Respondent. 8. The Petitioner is a generating company within the meaning of Section 2(28) of the Act, and is supplying power to Tamil Nadu, Rajasthan, and Chhattisgarh under long-term PPAs and is thus engaged under a composite scheme for the supply of power to more than one state. The Respondent is a trading licensee of this Commission. Therefore, this Commission has the jurisdiction to decide the present Petition under Section 79(1)(c) read with Section 79(1)(f) of the Act, 2003 and Section 19 of Act read with Regulations 9, 9. During the course of the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner made detailed oral submissions. After hearing the learned counsel, the Commission admitted the Petition and directed the Respondent to file its reply to the Petition, and the Petitioner may file its rejoinder thereafter. Respondent may comply with the direction dated 1.5.2024. The Commission, however, made it amply clear that such compliance by the Respondent, if any, will be without prejudice to its liability arising out of the non-compliance with the direction dated 1.5.2024 in the stipulated timeframe. - a) The Petitioner, even prior to filing the present Petition, has been simultaneously running parallel proceedings on the same cause of action, for recovery of the exact/ same amount as being pressed by way of the present Petition before different forums: b) The Respondent submitted that the CIRP process would leave the Respondent unable to honor its commitments to other stakeholders, effectively rendering the entire organization unviable. This simultaneous pursuit of remedies clearly highlights the duplicative and oppressive conduct of the Petitioner, which places an undue and inequitable burden on the Respondent. c) The Respondent has actively approached the Petitioner for a one-time settlement, offering the entire payment of principal in one go. Despite the attempts, the Petitioner still has not withdrawn any of the other cases being pursued against the Respondent, while the recovery is being constantly pressed. The Respondent has submitted that the Petitioner should settle the matter completely by giving an appropriate undertaking with respect to the withdrawal of all pending cases upon realization of the amount so directed by the Commission. e) The Respondent has requested that necessary directions be passed for amicable settlement of the matter under the aegis of this Commission, whereby parties can sit together and arrive at a full and final settlement, which results in payment to the Petitioner, while also ensuring withdrawal of all the cases. 19. After hearing the learned senior counsel and learned counsels for the parties, the Commission reserved the matters for order. 21. The Petitioner has submitted that it has learnt that the power supplied by the Petitioner was supplied onwards by the Respondent to Haryana Discoms and the Respondent has been paid in full amount by the Haryana Discoms for such supply, & despite this, the Respondent is not discharging its liability to the Petitioner. The Respondent, KEIPL, has submitted that it remains committed to resolving the dispute. However, the Petitioner’s pursuit of parallel proceedings is making redressal difficult. 22.
